import { z } from "zod";
import { TagSchema } from "@/lib/ai/tagging-schema";

/**
 * Lives outside the Server Action module so it can be unit-tested: a
 * "use server" file may only export async functions.
 *
 * Every field the tagger writes appears here. CLAUDE.md treats AI tags as a
 * draft, so a tag the model can set and the user cannot correct is a defect —
 * `colors` in particular feeds the generator's colour harmony scoring.
 *
 * `price` is the exception: the tagger never writes it (a photo cannot tell you
 * what something cost), so it is user-entered only. Nullable because most items
 * have no recorded price, and cost-per-wear must divide by nothing rather than
 * by a fabricated zero.
 */
export const UpdateSchema = z.object({
  name: z.string().nullable(),
  brand: z.string().nullable(),
  category: TagSchema.shape.category,
  subcategory: z.string().nullable(),
  colors: TagSchema.shape.colors,
  pattern: TagSchema.shape.pattern,
  material: TagSchema.shape.material,
  texture: TagSchema.shape.texture,
  formality: TagSchema.shape.formality,
  seasons: TagSchema.shape.seasons,
  price: z.number().nonnegative().nullable(),
});

1	import { z } from "zod";
2	
3	// MATERIALS and TEXTURES are defined HERE rather than imported from
4	// lib/closet/vocab.ts: vocab derives CATEGORIES/SEASONS from this schema, so
5	// importing back would be a cycle. `vocab.ts` re-exports these two, and remains
6	// the module every UI surface reads from.
7	
8	/**
9	 * What the garment is made of.
10	 *
11	 * `Merino wool` is listed separately from `Wool` on purpose: they behave
12	 * differently in heat, and one undifferentiated "wool" is exactly the
13	 * conflation that makes warmth rules wrong. Warmth is decided by fibre AND
14	 * construction — see TEXTURES.
15	 */
16	export const MATERIALS = [
17	  "Cotton",
18	  "Wool",
19	  "Merino wool",
20	  "Cashmere",
21	  "Linen",
22	  "Silk",
23	  "Denim",
24	  "Leather",
25	  "Suede",
26	  "Faux leather",
27	  "Canvas",
28	  "Corduroy",
29	  "Tweed",
30	  "Fleece",
31	  "Shearling",
32	  "Down",
33	  "Polyester",
34	  "Acrylic",
35	  "Nylon",
36	  "Viscose",
37	  "Modal",
38	  "Lyocell",
39	  "Stainless steel",
40	  "Gold",
41	  "Silver",
42	  "Rubber",
43	  "Other",
44	] as const;
45	
46	/**
47	 * How the fabric is built — knit structure and surface finish. A separate
48	 * dimension from material: a ribbed merino knit and a flat merino shirt share a
49	 * material and read completely differently, in both warmth and formality.
50	 *
51	 * `Other` is the escape hatch, and the one value deliberately shared with
52	 * MATERIALS. Without it a required `z.enum` forces the model to mislabel rather
53	 * than admit it cannot tell from a photo.
54	 */
55	export const TEXTURES = [
56	  "Flat",
57	  "Ribbed",
58	  "Cable knit",
59	  "Waffle",
60	  "Chunky knit",
61	  "Fine knit",
62	  "Brushed",
63	  "Fleece-back",
64	  "Twill",
65	  "Herringbone",
66	  "Quilted",
67	  "Pile",
68	  "Open knit",
69	  "Terry",
70	  "Seersucker",
71	  "Other",
72	] as const;
73	
74	// Categories + seasons match the prototype (Title case) so tags line up with
75	// the closet filters and the generator.
76	export const TagSchema = z.object({
77	  category: z.enum(["Tops", "Bottoms", "Outerwear", "Shoes", "Accessories", "Fragrance"]),
78	  subcategory: z.string().min(1),
79	  colors: z.array(z.string()).min(1).max(3),
80	  pattern: z.enum(["solid", "striped", "check", "print", "other"]),
81	  material: z.enum(MATERIALS),
82	  texture: z.enum(TEXTURES),
83	  formality: z.number().int().min(1).max(5),
84	  seasons: z.array(z.enum(["Spring", "Summer", "Autumn", "Winter"])).min(1),
85	});
86	export type Tags = z.infer<typeof TagSchema>;
87	
88	// Anthropic structured outputs (output_config.format) only accept type/enum/shape
89	// keywords — NOT the numeric (minimum/maximum/multipleOf), string (min/maxLength),
90	// or array (min/maxItems/uniqueItems) validation keywords that z.toJSONSchema()
91	// emits from our .min()/.max()/.int() refinements. Sending them 400s. We strip them
92	// here; the exact bounds are still enforced after the call by TagSchema.parse().
93	const UNSUPPORTED_JSON_SCHEMA_KEYWORDS = new Set([
94	  "minimum", "maximum", "exclusiveMinimum", "exclusiveMaximum", "multipleOf",
95	  "minLength", "maxLength",
96	  "minItems", "maxItems", "uniqueItems",
97	]);
98	
99	export function forStructuredOutput(node: unknown): unknown {
100	  if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.map(forStructuredOutput);
101	  if (node && typeof node === "object") {
102	    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
103	    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(node)) {
104	      if (UNSUPPORTED_JSON_SCHEMA_KEYWORDS.has(key)) continue;
105	      out[key] = forStructuredOutput(value);
106	    }
107	    // Structured outputs require every object to forbid extra properties.
108	    if (out.type === "object" && !("additionalProperties" in out)) {
109	      out.additionalProperties = false;
110	    }
111	    return out;
112	  }
113	  return node;
114	}
115	
116	// Zod 4 native JSON Schema, sanitised for Anthropic's output_config.format.
117	export const taggingJsonSchema = forStructuredOutput(
118	  z.toJSONSchema(TagSchema),
119	) as Record<string, unknown>;

-- items: one row per wardrobe piece. Categories match the prototype + closet filters.
create table public.items (
  id          uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id     uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  image_url   text not null,                 -- original (storage path)
  cutout_url  text,                           -- background-removed (storage path)
  name        text,                           -- e.g. "Brushed Oxford" (user-editable)
  brand       text,
  category    text not null check (category in ('Tops','Bottoms','Outerwear','Shoes','Accessories')),
  subcategory text,                           -- e.g. "Oxford shirt"
  colors      text[] not null default '{}',
  pattern     text,
  material    text,
  formality   int check (formality between 1 and 5),
  seasons     text[] default '{}',
  price       numeric,                         -- enables cost-per-wear later
  archived    boolean default false,
  created_at  timestamptz default now()
);
create index items_user_idx on public.items (user_id) where not archived;

alter table public.items enable row level security;

create policy "items_all_own"
  on public.items for all
  to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)
  with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);

-- private storage bucket; object paths are  <user_id>/<item_id>/<file>
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public)
  values ('wardrobe', 'wardrobe', false)
  on conflict (id) do nothing;

create policy "wardrobe_rw_own"
  on storage.objects for all
  to authenticated
  using (bucket_id = 'wardrobe' and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select auth.uid())::text)
  with check (bucket_id = 'wardrobe' and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select auth.uid())::text);

content.text:
Based on my analysis:

**Files reviewed:**
- `app/closet/[itemId]/actions.ts` — Server Action `updateItem` (RLS-scoped via `items_all_own` policy: `auth.uid() = user_id`)
- `lib/closet/update-schema.ts` — new Zod schema validating every field before DB write
- `components/closet/item-detail.tsx` — client caller
- `components/capture/confirm-form.tsx` — captures AI-draft edits (no direct sinks)
- `components/closet/color-picker.tsx` — enum-based picker
- `supabase/migrations/20260615114702_items.sql` — confirmed RLS policy uses `auth.uid()` for both `using` and `with check`

**Verified boundaries:**
- IDOR: `.eq("id", itemId)` is safe because Supabase RLS `items_all_own` policy enforces `auth.uid() = user_id` on `for all` (both `USING` and `WITH CHECK`). A foreign itemId matches 0 rows.
- Enum inputs (`category, colors, pattern, material, texture, formality, seasons`) all constrained via `TagSchema.shape.*`, matching CHECK constraints in Postgres.
